cells.tense: The momentum is gathered and the direction holds, and you are here with the pen.
cells.act: mark the good thing together, out loud
cells.ask: Something is standing because you held it. Say so out loud to the people who held it with you — once, plainly, the way you'd say a small fact. That's all the marking it needs.
cells.core: What you chose is holding, and you can tell that while you're in it. When something worth protecting comes under pressure, you gather what scattered and put it on one point, and stay there until it passes; now it has passed, and you're still facing the same way. Somebody built part of this with you, though — a hand, a word, someone who didn't drift off when it got quiet. Mark how it turned out, out loud, to them, once. Not a speech. The plain fact of it, said so it lands somewhere outside your own head, and then let them carry half of it. Things said in a room belong to the room; that is how they hold longer than the pressure did.
cells.sheetLine: The chosen ground is holding, and other people helped it hold.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a resistance that has not arrived, and the grip tightens ahead of it.
cells.ask: Take one hour where you stop adjusting for the next thing. No plan has to tighten, nothing has to come back right. Whatever the hour costs in readiness is the point of it.
cells.core: Whatever in you guards the chosen thing is braced for a push that hasn't come. So it keeps preparing: the position tightens, the worries sharpen, and the defending eats whatever made the choice worth making in the first place. Sheer holding on starts to look like the whole job. It isn't. The direction is settled; you don't have to keep rearranging it to feel that it's true. Give the guard a full hour with nothing to marshal. Say what comes back after that hour — the real answer is quieter than the braced one, and you can rest on it for the day, letting the hour end however it wants, with no conclusion.
cells.sheetLine: You are defending against a push that hasn't happened yet.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that the clearing has already left behind.
cells.act: keep what the change produced from drifting
cells.ask: Take one piece of what the change left — a way you now run a day, something you no longer do — and give it its ordinary upkeep, the small unglamorous kind.
cells.core: Where you hold a chosen direction, the clearing has already happened, and you're watching the old doorway for what it took. It shows up small: you answer from a day you no longer run, you reach to defend something that already fell, and the newer ground stays half-visited. The watching is real work; it's just aimed one room back. Hold onto one piece of what the change left you — how you run a day now, a thing you stopped doing — and keep it steady. Upkeep, not a victory. If it holds, the new ground starts holding you, and the doorway gets a little further behind.
cells.sheetLine: The clearing already happened and you are still watching the old doorway.

cells.tense: The clearing is already done and you have been reading it as something that happened to you.
cells.act: build the first new thing from what the clearing showed
cells.ask: From whatever the clearing showed, build the first piece of something new with your hands — not a plan for it, the first part of it — without stopping to name who is doing it.
cells.core: The ground is clear where the false thing fell, and you are already working it — deciding, arranging, starting — while your account says you just happened to be standing there. You are the one doing it. Not a spell that did the thinking, not waiting that finished it; you keep making the calls that put it back together. Build the first beginning from the clear ground: not a plan about it, the first piece of it, made with your hands. Let the making answer whose work this is. You won't have to announce anything. The thing will be there, and you'll know exactly whose it is.
cells.sheetLine: You are the one rebuilding, and calling it just luck.

attempts.check: The record supports Resolve as gathered momentum defending a chosen direction, seated where false structure is already clearing — but nothing in it says the person is mid-breakthrough personally, so any cell that places them inside a collapse they are living through would be overreach; the reader could reasonably say the clearing happened to circumstance, not to them, which is why the Unacknowledged ask builds something small and physical from whatever ground is already clear instead of trusting that a clearing is felt. The asks survive a wrong read — each is lawful to the medicine, useful in its own right, and none depends on the person recognising themselves in the picture. The sentence that serves the writer more than the reader is any line placing a verdict or a vigil inside them ('you have been bracing', 'you are still guarding it'); the Too Much cell keeps the bracing as a posture they could deny and still use the rest.
